label: When do adverse consequences accumulate against the possible absence of this foundation?
summary: See docs/notes/contingency-receptivity-c2.md#when-do-adverse-consequences-count-against-possible-absence. Grant that every populated accessible order has a root for existential giving and n is the only actual root in that respect. Any populated omission then requires a root that was actually dependent or a root outside the actual concrete inventory. Subtracting even many actual beings and changing their particular givers cannot suffice if all survivors remain dependent and no new root is admitted. A rational soul that essentially has participated being cannot itself supply such a root if participation requires another concrete giver. This leaves a replacement giver open. Complete records can exclude a backup switching on, a brute bearer where receipt is retained, or mere later persistence when n's indispensable origin is retained. Under a demanding knowledge-safety condition a very close, same-basis false belief about n challenges actual knowledge; empty and remote histories need produce no such error. A calibrated search can accumulate evidence against detectable accounts of P while missing another account entirely. High confidence in the restriction under its premises, moderate confidence in suspension about P. No new theorem or change to formal premises.
blocker: Root coverage throughout the alternatives, actual uniqueness and the admissibility of concrete emptiness or n-free realizations of the two populated cases remain open. A new root or a changed dependence status in a world that also contains n would not establish its possible absence. Credible accounts agreeing on creature evidence do not establish that an actual admissible pair differs about n. The chance of detecting an n-free history by the procedures used has no established calibration. Test a previously unexamined class of witnesses or a genuinely discriminatory feature of received existence before treating more cases as cumulative evidence.
